_comment: Single source of truth for role -> vendor/model/effort. Edit here, then run ~/.agents/bin/sync-agents. Orca coordinators read this to pick worker-start --agent/--model/--effort. 'prefer' is the default vendor for the role; 'fallback' is used when the preferred vendor is unavailable or when cross-review requires the other vendor. Pass the 'orca' block's values to worker-start.

policy.cross_review: Every artifact is reviewed by the OTHER vendor from the one that wrote it. Claude plans -> Codex checks the plan. Codex implements -> Claude reviews the diff. Claude implements -> Codex reviews the diff. High-risk: both vendors review in parallel and both must pass.
policy.risk_escalation: For high-risk work use the role's 'highRisk' override when one is defined. High-risk pairing: Claude side runs claude-opus-5-5, Codex side runs gpt-6.2-astra, both at high effort.
policy.watchers: Text-only mechanical work (worker) runs on Codex gpt-6-luna. Hands-on GUI/device testing (manual-tester) and PR watchers (implementer with PR: own) run on Codex gpt-6.1-terra. Fixes a watcher pushes still get a delta review by the other vendor.

opus.use: Most capable Claude model in use: planning, architecture (incl. high-risk), adversarial review (incl. high-risk, paired with gpt-6.2-astra).

astra.use: Most capable Codex model: high-risk implementation, architecture and review (paired with claude-opus-5-5), reviewing Claude-written code.

sol.use: Go-to coding model: standard implementation and plan checks.

terra.use: Efficient, strong at visual understanding and computer use: manual-tester (devices, screenshots, GUI) and PR watchers (babysit-pr owner).

researcher.description: Fact-finder. Use proactively before planning or whenever a task needs facts gathered from code, docs, logs or the web: locating code paths, tracing behaviour, comparing options, reading external docs. Returns cited findings, never recommendations or edits.

planner.description: Turns a goal plus research into an ordered, testable implementation plan. Use proactively for any change touching more than one file or component, before implementation starts. Writes the plan to a file and returns its path.

architect.description: Design gatekeeper. Use proactively to challenge a plan before implementation when it touches schemas/migrations, auth, money, crypto/signing, infra, public APIs or cross-component boundaries. Returns APPROVE or REVISE with numbered required changes. Never edits code.

plan-checker.description: Cross-vendor plan check for standard-tier work: reads a plan written by the other vendor, verifies its assumptions against the code, and returns APPROVE or REVISE. Lighter than architect. Never edits code.

implementer.description: Executes exactly one plan step or one well-specified change within its allowed paths, then proves it with tests/commands. Use for implementation work once the change is specified. Defers to project domain agents/skills for stack expertise.

watch._comment: PR-owner watcher started by /ship-pr (ROLE: implementer, PR: own). Use instead of the implementer's codex settings.

adversarial-reviewer.description: Adversarial reviewer. Use proactively after any non-trivial implementation and before a PR: tries to break the change (correctness, security, data/migration safety, missing tests) from the spec and diff alone. Returns CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE findings with repros. Never fixes.

worker.description: Cheap mechanical worker. Use proactively for bulk, low-judgement tasks: sweeps and inventories, renames, lint/format fixes, applying an already-decided pattern across files, scraping logs, running tests and summarising output. Escalates any judgement call instead of deciding.

manual-tester.description: Hands-on tester. Use to verify a change the way a person would: drive a device, emulator, app window or browser, capture screenshots and command output, and report PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED per check with evidence. Never edits project files.
